When there is an excess of supply (surplus), prices tend to fall as producers compete for consumers' business. Conversely, when there is an excess of demand (shortage), prices rise due to increased competition among buyers.

In summary, the relationship between supply and demand forms the basis of market economies, with price acting as a mechanism that balances production and consumption levels in response to changing conditions.
